the performance degradation is limited within 1.0 to 1.5dB for various TGn channel models, modulation and coding scheme, transmit antenna exciation schemes and OFDM-MIMO transceiver configurations, with a maximum CFO of 40 ppm.

the effects of CFO on the proposed IEEE 802 11 n WLAN system.

the proposed IEEE 802 11 n WLAN standard is able to mitigate the CFO effects with a maximum of 40 ppm CFO requirement.
the proposed IEEE 802 11 n standard can achieve the maximum CFO of 40 ppm without significant performance degradation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the residual CFO is a critical parameter that should be considered in the design of the MIMO OFDM system.
a CFO of 40 ppm is sufficient for the IEEE 802.16e standard, but a higher CFO is needed for the IEEE 800.11 n WLAN.
the proposed IEEE 80211 n WLAN system can tolerate the maximum CFO requirement specified in the standard without performance degradation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CFO mitigation in a MIMO OFDM WLAN system can be achieved by a simple frequency correction scheme without any additional hardware.
a CFO estimation scheme that is robust to both fine and coarse estimation errors is needed.

a CFO estimation scheme with a coarse CFO estimation error of 1 ppm and a fine CFO estimation error of less than 1/2 ppm is sufficient to meet the packet error rate requirement of the proposed IEEE 80211 n WLAN standard.
